subject: SLA template — uptime & latency remedies (Acme Cloud)
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2025-08-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: SLA amendment request — latency & credit cap

Naomi,

Thanks for the conversation last week. Attached is Acme Cloud's procurement team's formal ask on the SLA template for the Proof-of-Production deployment. Two quick points we need to confirm before procurement signs off:

1) Uptime: we need the SLA to reflect a single production uptime threshold of 99.900% (we understand this is lower than your standard but our traffic pattern and regional peering make the 99.95 target risky for us).

2) Remedies/credits: we must cap monthly service credits at 10% of the monthly invoice in any month where remedies are triggered. We cannot accept an open-ended cap higher than that.

Separately, Acme is also asking for a P95 inference latency commitment of 300ms for our primary inference route (region-us-west-2). If latency breaches occur, we'd expect a separate latency credit (not to be conflated with availability credits).

I've attached a short traffic report and our procurement template for reference. Can Redwood accept these two changes (99.900% uptime and 10% monthly credit cap) or propose a close compromise?

Regards,
Jane Doe
Head of Procurement, Acme Cloud
Attachments: SLA-request-acme-aug2025.pdf; traffic-report-q2.csv

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-19T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — latency & credit cap

Jane — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic data. Appreciate the context; sounds like a production-specific carveout is what you're looking for.

High-level response and a pragmatic proposal from Redwood:

- Uptime: our standard production SLA is 99.95% for Hosted instances. For the Acme production deployment we can offer a negotiated floor of 99.90% for the first 12 months post-cutover as a transitional exception, provided two conditions are met: (a) Acme agrees to a scheduled maintenance window of one 4-hour maintenance block per month for non-overlapping regional updates, and (b) Acme pins the model family and inference configuration (no frequent architecture changes) to allow kernel tuning.

- Latency: we can accept a separate latency SLO for P95 at 300ms scoped to the specified route. We treat latency breaches independently from availability incidents; remedies will be calculated from measured P95 windows.

- Remedies/Credits: Redwood's standard sliding remedy is 5%–25% of monthly invoice depending on the severity and duration of downtime. To meet Acme's request for a cap we propose a compromise: a 12% cap on monthly credits for availability shortfalls during the 12-month transitional period (instead of your 10%), with latency credits calculated separately and capped at 4% per month. That makes an aggregate theoretical cap of 16% but with clear separation between availability and latency buckets.

Why the uplift? The 2% delta protects both parties while preserving meaningful operational incentives for us to prevent regressions. We're open to revisiting the cap at the 12-month review.

I've attached a redlined SLA template (SLA-template-redwood-v2.pdf) that reflects the transitional uptime floor and the split credit buckets. Ben and Laura are on copy to confirm commercial alignment; we'll loop legal for final wording.

Next steps: if the transitional approach looks acceptable, Ben will send an updated commercial term and T&Cs; Laura will coordinate sign-off timeline with your procurement lead.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Attachments: SLA-template-redwood-v2.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecloud.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-19T14:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — latency & credit cap

Jane, Naomi — quick commercial touch:

Thanks Naomi for the pragmatic framing. From a deal math perspective, we can live with the 12% availability cap during the 12-month transition, provided we get the following in writing from Acme:

- Agreement to the monthly 4-hour maintenance window (non-negotiable operational requirement).
- Commitment to an initial minimum throughput/commitment level (monthly spend threshold) for the Dedicated pool so that we can reserve capacity accordingly.

On latency credits: separating them makes sense operationally, but to be explicit — latency credits will only be applied to requests within the defined route/tag and will be measured on rolling 7-day windows. We recommend the latency cap be 3% instead of 4% to keep aggregate exposure lower.

If Acme accepts the maintenance and minimum spend, I can update pricing (and ingestion credits) and push DocuSign with the revised cap numbers. Laura — can you confirm timing for procurement sign-off if they accept 12%/3% split?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecloud.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-20T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — latency & credit cap (legal redline highlights)

Hi all — looping in with legal redline highlights after reviewing Naomi's proposed transitional wording. Main items we'd like on record: 

1) Carveouts: we will include explicit third-party network and cloud provider outage carveouts (we'll propose language that credits only incidents where Redwood's control plane and serving runtime are demonstrably the root cause).

2) Maintenance: the monthly 4-hour maintenance block must be scheduled in advance with a 7-day notice and cannot be used as a repeated mechanism to avoid remedies. We'll add a maximum of two discretionary deferrals per quarter.

3) Measurement windows: availability calculations will continue to use calendar-month aggregation but latency remedy windows will be measured on a rolling 7-day P95 basis. Both definitions will be explicitly instrumented via our observability hooks (links to shared dashboards will be provided).

4) Cap mechanics: we agree in principle to a temporary 12% availability cap and a 3% latency cap (Ben's suggestion), but legal prefers a single absolute cap on remedies from Redwood per month, stated as percentage of invoice, with internal sub-bucket limits described for transparency. This reduces ambiguity for accounting. If Acme insists on fully separate pools, we'll need to reflect that in invoicing attachments.

Please review the attached redlines in Drive (link above). If Acme is aligned, we will prepare a DocuSign packet with the transitional language and a one-year review clause. 

Tessa Morgan
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Tessa.Morgan@redwood.com
Attachments: none
